correctness.rationale: The graph has n row cliques of size n-1 and one reversal bond for each unordered pair. Writing row spin sums r_i and b doubly-down reversal pairs gives the exact identity H/J=-n(n-1)+sum_i[r_i^2/2+(1-x)r_i]+4b for every spin configuration. Parity restrictions on r_i make the rowwise minimizers exactly the claimed nonnegative k except at the even-n zero plateau. For each permitted k, a k-regular graph on n labels exists (nk even); its complement is even-regular, admits Eulerian orientation, and produces b=0 and equal row sums k. A perfect matching plus Eulerian orientation gives the even-n zero plateau; the odd-n x=0 tie is resolved by b=0 implying nonnegative magnetization. These constructions attain every lower bound and certify all critical equality conditions. Independent full spin-state enumeration for n=3,4 and multiple half-integer/critical fields agreed; n=5 was covered in source code but not independently enumerated in this execution.
residual_risks: No independent exhaustive check beyond n=4; the all-n conclusion rests on the described graph-theoretic proof, not finite experiments.

value.rationale: An all-order exact zero-temperature magnetization classification of a geometrically motivated frustrated graph family is a natural nontrivial structural result. It explains a parity-forced different onset field, gives every finite-field plateau and all critical equality cases by a new Euler-orientation realization rather than a single numerical graph census; the known n=4 point is correctly credited. No thermodynamic or finite-temperature extension is claimed.
residual_risks: Physical significance is confined to exactly uniform exchange and classical finite zero-temperature ground states.

final_claim: For each n>=3, the uniform classical antiferromagnetic Ising model on the clique truncation of K_n has an exact all-field zero-temperature energy envelope, parity-dependent transition fields 2,4,...,n-1 for odd n and 1,3,...,n-1 for even n, and a complete equality-condition description of ground-state sectors.
